eyebrow: International comparator · finite health after childbirth-injury repair
program: Conditional whole-organization value of a $100,000 unrestricted gift

nutshell.headline: Repair can relieve severe chronic disability; additional access and duration drive whole-gift value.
nutshell.body: Conditional central donor cost is $76,286 and gross resource cost $101,944 per 10 overseas QALYs. These are explicit best-estimate assumptions, not a measured unrestricted-gift result or guarantee of room. Total central is above the $100k screen; no parameter was retuned to pass.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: A focused organization finances surgical access through local partners. Durable continence improvements have observational support.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: No preference-utility or current marginal waiting-time study anchors the key bridge. Partial recovery, repeat operations, donor replacement and non-fistula costs materially reduce credit.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Current incremental capacity/funding gap unknown. Validate unique patients, marginal spending, alternative treatment timing and outcomes before committing.

summary.label: Central total / 10 QALYs
summary.detail: $76,286 donor; 13.109 net overseas QALYs per $100,000 whole gift. Total central narrowly misses the $100k screen.

summary.label: SF / Bay direct health
summary.detail: No finite positive local ratio. Indirect effects unknown and uncredited, not asserted absent.

summary.label: Matched whole cost
summary.detail: 2024 whole expense/output ratio, then explicit 1.25 marginal/current cost prior; no second overhead factor.

summary.label: Current funding room
summary.detail: Prior 50% funding additionality is not proof of a ready unfunded tranche.

programSection.body: General support pays for the complete organizational system; only the fistula-repair clinical stream is quantified. Perineal tears, training and network effects receive no separate benefit credit.

steps.title: Keep every dollar
steps.detail: Whole historical expenses include program, management and fundraising; expansion cost uplift remains explicit.

steps.title: Deduplicate and allocate
steps.detail: Count distinct care episodes, then fistula share. Other operations still cost money.

steps.title: Compare with available care
steps.detail: Financial additionality and finite waiting-time advantage remove different counterfactuals.

steps.title: Value finite health
steps.detail: Signed utility by disjoint recovery states, survival, decay and one discount; subtract separate harms.

programSection.boundary: No life saved, newborn health, lifetime 40-year cure, income-to-QALY or DALY=QALY shortcut.

model.headline: A finite morbidity stream with the whole gift retained
model.body: 67.269 nominal surgeries × .85 unique episodes × .50 additionality = 28.589 added episodes. Of these, 22.872 are modeled fistula cases.

equation.label: Whole-gift health bridge
equation.expression: N = gift / (whole annual expense / annual surgery count × marginal-cost multiplier); E = N × unique share × funding additionality. Q = E × fistula share × (pDry×uDry + pPartial×uPartial) × finite discounted survival/decay years − E×procedure harm − independent harm.

inputs.label: expense per surgery 2024
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Matched 2024 whole expenses / all reported surgeries; includes administration, fundraising, training, outreach and tears. Accounting average, not causal marginal quote.

inputs.label: marginal cost multiplier
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: 2024-to-2026 prices, remote/complex expansion and accounting/output mismatch; not estimated inflation. No second overhead haircut.

inputs.label: unique patient fraction
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Reported surgeries may include repeats; only unique care episodes receive first-treatment outcome stream; repeat surgery remains fully costed.

inputs.label: fistula fraction
inputs.confidence: Current provider reports 20% tear cases; working share .8, range .6–.9
inputs.best: Current provider reports 20% tear cases; working share .8, range .6–.9
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Do not apply fistula trial outcomes to perineal tears. Their costs and potential benefits retained/uncredited.

inputs.label: financial additionality
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Capacity added beyond public hospitals, NGOs, reserves and donor replacement. Not patient waiting-time catch-up. Current room unknown.

inputs.label: dry fraction / partial fraction
inputs.confidence: Conservative full operated cohort anchor 21/44 dry, 13/44 partial; favorable transfer .75/.20
inputs.best: Conservative full operated cohort anchor 21/44 dry, 13/44 partial; favorable transfer .75/.20
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Nielsen: 38/44 followed, 37 classified urinary states. All 10 others receive zero durable health (3 persistent, 6 lost, 1 unclassified). No RCT or current portfolio rate. Cautious .4/.3 is a joint transfer scenario, not a lower confidence bound on both fractions.

inputs.label: dry utility gain / partial utility gain
inputs.confidence: Explicit preference-utility priors .25/.08, ranges .1–.35 / 0–.15, signed -0.1/-.05 diagnostics
inputs.best: Explicit preference-utility priors .25/.08, ranges .1–.35 / 0–.15, signed -0.1/-.05 diagnostics
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: QoL questionnaires and DALY disability weights are not direct QALYs. Recovery does not imply restored social health; no separate mental-health or income credit.

inputs.label: advantage years
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Hard cap on advantage over later public/NGO treatment or recovery, not patient lifetime; actual no-gift waiting-time distribution unavailable.

inputs.label: delay years / annual mortality / annual effect decay
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Delay to care, finite survival and recurrence/declining effect after long-term outcome anchor. No lifetime extension or maternal-death benefit.

inputs.label: procedure harm q
inputs.confidence: Prior .015 per added distinct episode; range0–.1
inputs.best: Prior .015 per added distinct episode; range0–.1
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Gift-date PV total acute harms from every operation/repeat in an added unique episode, including tears; not a per-operation rate. Excludes durable-state worsening. Full present harm without subtracting delayed alternative repair harm is conservative.

inputs.label: independent harm q
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Gift-date PV health loss outside patient treatment stream, e.g. displaced other scarce care; no activity multiplier. Do not double count procedure harm.

inputs.label: external resource per nominal surgery
inputs.range: See labeled numeric range in confidence; null/harm cases below
inputs.basis: Unreimbursed public hospital/noncash staff, patient travel/time, family care, including unsuccessful/repeat/tear procedures. Add on all nominal surgery equivalents. Gross resources, not net induced societal spending.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Scenarios are not confidence intervals. Central is conditional, not probability-weighted certainty. Correcting missing outcomes to failure raises central total above $100k without retuning. Cautious total $25.49m; one-year catch-up $500,923; favorable $8,229. Zero and negative health retain full costs and suppress positive ratios.
model.fundingBoundary: No verified unfunded 2026 tranche. Positive prior permits research ranking, not a guarantee a gift adds care. Public capacity and other NGOs are baseline. Independent donor displacement and eventual patient catch-up are different counterfactuals.
model.giftHeading: Where the whole $100,000 unrestricted gift goes

evidence.result: Reported long-term dry/partial/persistent states support incomplete recovery.
evidence.transfer: Small uncontrolled cohort, loss to follow-up and portfolio differences; no direct QALY measurement.

evidence.result: Substantial ongoing poor quality of life reported.
evidence.transfer: Do not assume surgical closure restores full social or mental health.

evidence.result: Matched historical full cost $1,189 per reported surgery.
evidence.transfer: Accounting grant timing and repeat cases mean not current marginal price; uplift and unique share are priors.

reservations: Clinical outcome and utility transfer are not randomized evidence of this donor gift.
Five-year treatment advantage and 50% financial additionality are the decisive unmeasured priors.
Annual expense/output ratio may mismatch grant accrual and surgical delivery; current marginal multiplier addresses this only provisionally.
Zero credit for perineal tears is an evidence exclusion, not proof they have no benefit; their procedure harms and full resource costs remain.
Gross resource envelope adds outside resources to nominal activity even under funding replacement. It is not net induced public expenditure or net societal cost.
excludedBenefits: Training and future surgical capacity beyond modeled episodes
Income, caregiver relief and social benefits outside the utility bridge
SF/Bay indirect knowledge, altruism or spillover health
